_note: THE ROOT PLAN — the ordered first-ready fold that replaces the boot.json two-arm rule (root-plan.md). `App.json entry.surfaces` is a non-empty ordered array of candidates (`"X"` ≡ `{view:"X"}`; candidate keys: view, config, timeoutMs, id — there is deliberately NO onFailure/policy key: failure ALWAYS advances, an exhausted list is the only stop). NORMALIZATION (pinned by `expect.normalized`): scalar shorthand expands; timeoutMs defaults to the kernel constant ROOT_SETTLE_TIMEOUT_MS = 15000 (identical on every runtime); id defaults to the view name, and when a view occurs more than once in the plan every DERIVED id for it is numbered `view#k` (k = 1-based occurrence among candidates sharing that view) while EXPLICIT ids ride verbatim and never renumber the derived ones. FOLD SEMANTICS: candidates run in array order; each attempt mounts as ordinary frame-0 content (config rides the mount VERBATIM as component attributes — moustache values resolve in the existing attribute plane at real mount, outside this corpus); the attempt then races the frame-settle signal (`screen.ready` for frame 0) against root-attributed failure against its deadline. ready → fire `root.ready` once, the plan is DONE for the process lifetime (later signals of any kind are dropped — no silent root swap; recovery is module/route-owned). failed → fire `root.failed` and advance unconditionally. list exhausted → fire `root.exhausted` and show the kernel boot diagnostic (kernel-owned pixels, not a component). FAILURE ATTRIBUTION: a failure is a `dsx.error` carrying origin "root" delivered while the attempt is live; errors with any other origin NEVER advance the plan; a candidate whose view is not in the build's component registry fails at mount with code `root.component_missing` (reachable only when build validation was bypassed — V2 aborts this at prepare); a deadline expiry synthesizes code `root.timeout` through the same error plane. SIMULATION CONTRACT (how every runner drives these cases): a virtual clock starts at 0; attempt 0 mounts at t=0 and attempt N+1 mounts at the instant attempt N fails; deadline = mountAt + timeoutMs; events are delivered in atMs order, but a live attempt whose deadline ≤ the next event's atMs times out FIRST (at the deadline instant), and after the last event a still-live attempt times out at its deadline — the fold always terminates; an event carrying the optional `attempt` field (index into the normalized plan) belongs to that attempt and is delivered only while that attempt is live, else DROPPED — the stale-token rule; `settle` without `attempt` settles the live attempt; `error` events carry `origin` + `code` and without `attempt` apply to the live attempt (attribution still requires origin "root"). CASE FIELDS: `components` = the build's registered component tags (the registry double — membership is the ONLY thing it asserts); `surfaces` = the RAW pre-normalization entry.surfaces value; `events` = the signal script; `expect` = { normalized (the full normalized plan; entries list `config` only when non-empty), attempts (attempt ids in order), failures ([{id, code}] in order), ready (id or null), fired (the COMPLETE ordered list of root.* emissions — a dropped signal adds nothing), diagnostic (bool: the exhaustion diagnostic shows), winnerView (optional: the boot winner that view-less route rows now follow), mountedAttrs (optional map id → the attribute bag the mount received, asserted verbatim) }. Executors (all three drive the REAL extracted engine — RootPlanFold / RootPlan.Fold — through the Host seam on this virtual clock; the PRODUCTION wiring around it is pinned separately by each runtime's boot integration tests): TS `OpenSource/Web/packages/dom/test/router-conformance.test.ts` (+ `boot-integration` for the bootDsx wiring) · Kotlin `Engine/Android :core RootPlanConformanceTest` (+ RouterTest's real-boot case) · Swift `RootPlanConformance` in `Engine/iOS/ConformanceHosts.swift` is the REFERENCE (RecordMain, conformance-record lane). boot.json and `bootsToEntryFallback` are RETIRED on every lane — this corpus owns the boot.
